title: Propensity-Score Matching – Treated vs Control
text:
Treated (ICI, n=379) and control (non-ICI neoplasm, n=1,307) cohorts differ on demographics, calendar era, comorbidity profile, baseline kidney function, and — critically for outcome interpretation — baseline creatinine surveillance intensity (n_cre_pre_1yr). A direct comparison would confound the ICI effect with differential measurement, follow-up, and practice-era effects. Propensity-score matching is used to construct a comparable control subset while retaining all 379 treated patients.










Parameter
Value




Matching algorithm
Nearest-neighbor PS matching (logit PS), greedy, no replacement


Ratio
Variable 1:k, ratio = 2 (target mean), min.controls = 1, max.controls = 3


Caliper
0.2 × SD(logit PS)


Exact-match stratum
era (2016–2019 / 2020–2023)


Eligibility filter
has_pre_cre == 1


Seed
set.seed(42)


Software
R MatchIt 4.x


Balance target
Standardized mean difference (SMD) < 0.1 for all PS model covariates






The 04092026 RPDR pull is pre-curated — the source Dem.txt already contains exactly 1,307 patients who satisfy every cohort-build inclusion criterion. The control pipeline filters re-confirm but do not drop additional rows.



Step (executed in control_group.qmd)
n




1. Unique EMPIs in mes98_040726114217167239_Dem.txt
1,307


2. Has neoplasm Dx (ICD10 C00–D49) → defines Index_date
1,307


3. Has post-index CRE (last_cre_days > 0)
1,307


4. Has CRE within 12 months pre-index
1,307


5. ≥ 18 months (548 d) follow-up
1,307


6. ≥ 2 post-index CRE measurements
1,307


7. Non-missing baseline CRE (90-d window)
1,307


8. eGFR_CRE_baseline ≥ 10
1,307









Step
Control n




Eligible cohort after control_group.qmd build
1,307


Drop Index year ≤ 2015 (no treated counterpart)
−338 → 969


Drop has_pre_cre == 0
(computed in §3)


Eligible for matching
see chunk cohort-restrict













Choice
Reason




Drop pre-2016 controls
Treated cohort begins 2016; earlier controls have no temporal counterpart


Variable 1:k matching with ratio=2, min.controls=1, max.controls=3
Allows up to 1:3 in the early era where controls are abundant; falls back to 1:1 in the late era (2020–2023) where controls are scarce. Keeps all 379 eligible treated patients in the matched cohort.


Caliper 0.2 × SD(logit PS)
Austin (2011) — empirically optimal for bias removal


Exact-match on era only
Era shift is large/structural; sex balances adequately via PS alone


Include n_cre_pre_1yr in PS model
Surveillance intensity is a study-specific candidate confounder; must be balanced explicitly


Use binary white (1 = White, 0 = other) instead of multi-level Race
≥96% of both cohorts are White; treating Race as a 4-level factor wastes degrees of freedom on near-empty cells. The binary form captures all of the between-group variation that exists.


Exclude Ethnic_Group from PS model
Highly collinear with Race/white after harmonisation and contributes little independent variation


Exclude pre_history_days from PS model
Largely redundant with n_cre_pre_1yr; including both inflates the PS model without improving balance


Exclude Cancer_Diagnosis / Cancers_stage
Control cohort lacks these fields (only treated has them)


Exclude pre_median_HGB_90days, pre_median_ALB_90days from PS model
High missingness in controls (routine pre-ICI oncology workup labs are rarely drawn in the control pool); presence would leak treatment status. Shown in Table 1 for transparency only


Exclude post-exposure variables (last_cre_days, aki, outcomes)
Would induce collider bias if included






Within the 2020–2023 stratum the eligible counts are roughly 1:1.4 (treated 142 vs control 192), so a fixed 1:3 match is structurally infeasible — there simply aren’t 426 controls available. The variable-ratio specification handles this automatically:

2016–2019 era: target up to 1:3 (control supply is plentiful at 777).
2020–2023 era: most treated patients will receive 1:1 matches because min.controls = 1 is the binding constraint once the closest controls are consumed.

This is the right behaviour for this study — it preserves all treated patients, keeps the closest-PS controls in each era, and accepts a smaller k where the data demand it. The downstream Cox / competing-risk model uses subclass-clustered SEs (or MatchIt weights), so unequal cluster sizes are handled correctly.







NotePrerequisite



Before rendering this page, re-render treated_group.qmd and control_group.qmd so the new n_cre_pre_1yr, pre_history_days, has_pre_cre, cre_rate_pre, n_cre_post, cre_rate_post columns are present in the output .xlsx files.

title: CKD after ICI – Project Summary
text:
Clinical research analysis of long-term kidney outcomes after immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy — CKD incidence, progression, and ESKD over 10-year follow-up.
This website contains three components:

Analysis — Main cohort analysis (full pipeline + models)
Treated Group — ICI-treated cohort data build + Table 1
Control Group — Non-ICI cancer control cohort data build + Table 1
Matching — Propensity-score matching of treated vs control with balance diagnostics
Results — Outcome analyses on matched cohort: CIF, Fine-Gray, cause-specific Cox, 5-yr logistic for all CKD/ESKD outcomes

3.2 pre_lab_median_year
Gets the median CRE in a 90-day window around each yearly mark post-index. Also finds the closest lab value up to that yearly mark as a fallback. Falls back to the closest value if no labs exist in the 90-day window.

pre_lab_median_year <- function(data, year, days, index_date, Group_Id) {
  index_date <- enquo(index_date)

  last_offset  <- year * 365
  first_offset <- last_offset - days

  median_name      <- paste0("pre_median_", Group_Id, "_", year, "year")
  lab_num_name     <- paste0("lab_num_", year, "year")
  closest_name     <- paste0("closest_", Group_Id, "_", year, "year")
  closest_date_name <- paste0("closest_", Group_Id, "_", year, "year_date")

  median <- data %>%
    filter(Group_Id == !!Group_Id, grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Result)) %>%
    mutate(Result = as.numeric(Result)) %>%
    filter(Seq_Date_Time >= (!!index_date + first_offset),
           Seq_Date_Time <= !!index_date + last_offset) %>%
    group_by(EMPI) %>%
    summarise(
      !!median_name := median(Result, na.rm = TRUE),
      !!lab_num_name := n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  closest <- data %>%
    filter(Group_Id == !!Group_Id, grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Result)) %>%
    mutate(Result = as.numeric(Result)) %>%
    filter(Seq_Date_Time <= !!index_date + last_offset) %>%
    arrange(EMPI, desc(Seq_Date_Time)) %>%
    distinct(EMPI, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    rename(!!closest_name := Result,
           !!closest_date_name := Seq_Date_Time) %>%
    select(EMPI, !!index_date, !!closest_name, !!closest_date_name)

  result <- median %>%
    merge(closest, by = "EMPI", all = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      !!median_name := ifelse(is.na(!!sym(median_name)),
                              !!sym(closest_name),
                              !!sym(median_name))
    ) %>%
    select(EMPI, !!median_name, !!lab_num_name)

  return(result)
}

3.6 create_outcome_table
Generates a gtsummary Table 1 for a given year suffix, filtering to patients who survived to that landmark.

create_outcome_table <- function(data, time_suffix) {

  year_num <- as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9]", "", time_suffix))
  stage_history_cols <- paste0("ckd_stage_", 1:year_num, "year")

  survival_col     <- paste0("survival_", time_suffix)
  ckd_inc_col      <- paste0("ckd_incidence_", time_suffix)
  ckd_prog_col     <- paste0("ckd_progression_", time_suffix)
  eskd_comp_col    <- paste0("eskd_composite_", time_suffix)
  ckd_comp_col     <- paste0("ckd_composite_", time_suffix)

  data %>%
    filter(.data[[survival_col]] == 1) %>%
    select(
      ## Demographics
      Age, male, Race, Ethnic_Group,
      ## Outcomes (dynamic)
      all_of(ckd_inc_col), all_of(ckd_prog_col),
      all_of(eskd_comp_col), all_of(ckd_comp_col),
      ## Longitudinal CKD Stages (cumulative up to year X)
      all_of(stage_history_cols),
      ckd_stage_baseline,
      aki,
      ## Comorbidities
      dm, htn, cad, cirrhosis,
      ## Medications
      ace_arb, diu, ppi, steroids, smoking, statins,
      ICI_Class, nephrotoxic_chemo,
      ## Labs / Kidney function
      pre_CRE_180days, pre_HGB_180days, pre_ALB_180days,
      eGFR_CRE_baseline
    ) %>%
    tbl_summary(missing_text = "Missing")
}

3.7 pre_lab (closest value — Cystatin C style)
Finds the closest lab value on or before index_date within the time window. Returns one row per patient (most recent qualifying lab result).

Uses Seq_Date_Time for filtering and sorting (bug-fixed version from Cystatin C pipeline).


pre_lab <- function(data, month, time, index_date, Group_Id) {
  index_date <- enquo(index_date)
  if (month) {
    time_value <- time * 30
  } else {
    time_value <- time
  }

  lab_name      <- paste0("pre_", Group_Id, "_", time_value, "days")
  lab_date_name <- paste0("pre_", Group_Id, "_", time_value, "days_date")

  result <- data %>%
    filter(Group_Id == !!Group_Id, grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Result)) %>%
    mutate(Result = as.numeric(Result)) %>%
    filter(Seq_Date_Time >= (!!index_date) - time_value,
           Seq_Date_Time <= !!index_date) %>%
    arrange(EMPI, desc(Seq_Date_Time)) %>%
    distinct(EMPI, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    rename(!!lab_name := Result,
           !!lab_date_name := Seq_Date_Time) %>%
    select(EMPI, !!lab_name, !!lab_date_name)

  return(result)
}

3.9 cmp_variable (competing risk)
Builds competing-risk time and status for a single outcome. Status coding: 0 = censored, 1 = event occurred, 2 = death (competing event).

cmp_variable <- function(data, event_time, event_status, name) {
  event_time   <- enquo(event_time)
  event_status <- enquo(event_status)

  cmp_time_name   <- paste0("cmp_time_", name)
  cmp_status_name <- paste0("cmp_status_", name)

  data %>%
    mutate(
      !!cmp_time_name   := ifelse(time_to_death <= !!event_time, time_to_death, !!event_time),
      !!cmp_status_name := ifelse(time_to_death <= !!event_time, time_to_death_status, !!event_status)
    )
}

3.10 make_ckd_outcome_date (sustained eGFR-based outcomes)
Identifies sustained (≥ days_threshold) episodes where a condition is met. Returns one row per patient with binary flag + first qualifying date.

make_ckd_outcome_date <- function(data, id_var, date_var, condition_expr,
                                   days_threshold = 90, outcome_name = "default") {
  id_var      <- enquo(id_var)
  date_var    <- enquo(date_var)
  cond_q      <- enquo(condition_expr)
  outcome_sym <- ensym(outcome_name)
  outcome_date_name <- paste0(outcome_name, "_date")

  working <- data %>%
    arrange(!!id_var, !!date_var) %>%
    group_by(!!id_var) %>%
    mutate(
      .cond   = if_else(!!cond_q, 1L, 0L),
      .change = .cond != lag(.cond, default = first(.cond)),
      .run    = cumsum(.change)
    )

  episodes <- working %>%
    group_by(!!id_var, .run) %>%
    summarise(
      .code = first(.cond),
      .start = first(!!date_var),
      .last  = last(!!date_var),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(!!id_var) %>%
    mutate(
      .end  = lead(.start),
      .end  = if_else(is.na(.end), .last, .end),
      .days = as.integer(.end - .start)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  episodes %>%
    filter(!is.na(.days)) %>%
    group_by(!!id_var) %>%
    summarise(
      has_event  = any(.code == 1L & .days >= days_threshold, na.rm = TRUE),
      event_date = if (any(.code == 1L & .days >= days_threshold, na.rm = TRUE)) {
        min(.start[.code == 1L & .days >= days_threshold], na.rm = TRUE)
      } else {
        as.Date(NA)
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(!!outcome_sym := as.integer(has_event)) %>%
    rename(!!outcome_date_name := event_date) %>%
    select(-has_event)
}

dpp4i    <- med_list(data = master_med, names = dpp4i_names, index_date = Index_date)
sglt2i   <- med_list(data = master_med, names = sglt2i_names, index_date = Index_date)

# Diagnoses
esrd_kt <- dia_list_icd(master_dia, icd_code = esrd_kt_codes, index_date = Index_date)
esrd_kt_after_ici <- dia_list_icd_after_index(master_dia, icd_code = esrd_kt_codes,
                                               index_date = Index_date) %>%
  rename(esrd_kt_after_ici_date = first_event_date)
dm  <- dia_list_icd(master_dia, icd_code = diabetes_codes, index_date = Index_date)
htn <- dia_list_icd(master_dia, icd_code = htn_codes, excluded_names = no_htn_list,
                    med_data = master_med, med_names = htn_med_list,
                    index_date = Index_date)
cad <- dia_list_name(master_dia, listed_names = cad_list, index_date = Index_date)
cirrhosis <- master_dia %>%
  filter(Date <= Index_date) %>%
  filter(grepl("cirrhosis", Diagnosis_Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  distinct(EMPI)
smoking <- master_dia %>%
  filter(grepl(paste(smoking_list, collapse = "|"), Diagnosis_Name, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  distinct(EMPI)

# Join all comorbidities/medications to final_master
final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    diu      = ifelse(EMPI %in% diu$EMPI, 1, 0),
    ace_arb  = ifelse(EMPI %in% ace_arb$EMPI, 1, 0),
    esrd_kt  = ifelse(EMPI %in% esrd_kt$EMPI, 1, 0),
    esrd_kt_after_ici = ifelse(EMPI %in% esrd_kt_after_ici$EMPI, 1, 0),
    dm       = ifelse(EMPI %in% dm$EMPI, 1, 0),
    htn      = ifelse(EMPI %in% htn$EMPI, 1, 0),
    ppi      = ifelse(EMPI %in% ppi$EMPI, 1, 0),
    steroids = ifelse(EMPI %in% steroids$EMPI, 1, 0),
    smoking  = ifelse(EMPI %in% smoking$EMPI, 1, 0),
    cad      = ifelse(EMPI %in% cad$EMPI, 1, 0),
    cirrhosis = ifelse(EMPI %in% cirrhosis$EMPI, 1, 0),
    statins  = ifelse(EMPI %in% statins$EMPI, 1, 0),
    dpp4i    = ifelse(EMPI %in% dpp4i$EMPI, 1, 0),
    sglt2i   = ifelse(EMPI %in% sglt2i$EMPI, 1, 0)
  )

# Merge esrd_kt_after_ici date
final_master <- final_master %>%
  merge(esrd_kt_after_ici, by = "EMPI", all.x = TRUE)

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
text:
5.4 ICI_Class & nephrotoxic_chemo

final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    ICI_Class = case_when(
      ICI_Name %in% c("pembrolizumab", "nivolumab", "cemiplimab",
                       "Nivolumab", "Dostarlimab", "Cemiplimab") ~ "PD1",
      ICI_Name %in% c("atezolizumab", "avelumab", "durvalumab") ~ "PDL1",
      ICI_Name == "ipilimumab" ~ "CTLA4",
      ICI_Name == "ipilimumab AND nivolumab" ~ "Combination",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    nephrotoxic_chemo = if_else(
      if_any(
        any_of(c("Bevacizumab", "Cisplatin", "Carboplatin", "Pemetrexed",
                  "Gemcitabine", "Cetuximab", "Trastuzumab")),
        ~ . == 1
      ),
      1L, 0L
    )
  )

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
text:
6.2 Baseline eGFR & CKD stage

final_master$eGFR_CRE_baseline <- mapply(
  gfr_calc,
  final_master$pre_median_CRE_90days,
  final_master$male,
  final_master$Age
)

final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    ckd_stage_baseline = case_when(
      eGFR_CRE_baseline >= 90                           ~ 1,
      eGFR_CRE_baseline >= 60 & eGFR_CRE_baseline < 90 ~ 2,
      eGFR_CRE_baseline >= 30 & eGFR_CRE_baseline < 60 ~ 3,
      eGFR_CRE_baseline >= 15 & eGFR_CRE_baseline < 30 ~ 4,
      eGFR_CRE_baseline < 15                            ~ 5
    ),
    ckd_stage_baseline_3 = case_when(
      ckd_stage_baseline == 1  ~ "stage 1",
      ckd_stage_baseline == 2  ~ "stage 2",
      ckd_stage_baseline >= 3  ~ "stage 3 or more"
    )
  )

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
section: 6.3 CKD outcomes from RPDR Lab (sustained eGFR-based)
text:
6.3 CKD outcomes from RPDR Lab (sustained eGFR-based)

# Build post-baseline eGFR series for each patient
outcome_labs <- master_lab %>%
  select(EMPI, Seq_Date_Time, Result, Group_Id, Index_date) %>%
  merge(final_master %>% select(EMPI, pre_median_CRE_90days, eGFR_CRE_baseline,
                                 male, Age),
        by = "EMPI") %>%
  filter(Group_Id == "CRE", grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Result)) %>%
  mutate(Result = as.numeric(Result)) %>%
  filter(Seq_Date_Time > Index_date) %>%
  mutate(eGFR_CRE = mapply(gfr_calc, Result, male, Age)) %>%
  select(EMPI, eGFR_CRE_baseline, eGFR_CRE, eGFR_CRE_date = Seq_Date_Time) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_drop = round((eGFR_CRE_baseline - eGFR_CRE) / eGFR_CRE_baseline, 3)
  ) %>%
  arrange(EMPI, eGFR_CRE_date)

# CKD incidence: >25% drop AND eGFR <60, from baseline >=60, sustained >=90 days
ckd_incidence <- make_ckd_outcome_date(
  data = outcome_labs, id_var = EMPI, date_var = eGFR_CRE_date,
  condition_expr = pct_drop > 0.25 & eGFR_CRE < 60 & eGFR_CRE_baseline >= 60,
  days_threshold = 90, outcome_name = "ckd_incidence"
)

# ESKD definition 1: eGFR <10 sustained >=90 days
eskd_defination_1 <- make_ckd_outcome_date(
  data = outcome_labs, id_var = EMPI, date_var = eGFR_CRE_date,
  condition_expr = eGFR_CRE < 10,
  days_threshold = 90, outcome_name = "eskd_defination_1"
)

# CKD progression: >30% drop from baseline <60, sustained >=90 days
ckd_progression <- make_ckd_outcome_date(
  data = outcome_labs, id_var = EMPI, date_var = eGFR_CRE_date,
  condition_expr = pct_drop > 0.30 & eGFR_CRE_baseline < 60,
  days_threshold = 90, outcome_name = "ckd_progression"
)

# Merge outcomes
final_master <- final_master %>%
  merge(ckd_incidence, by = "EMPI", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  merge(eskd_defination_1, by = "EMPI", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  merge(ckd_progression, by = "EMPI", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    ckd_incidence      = replace_na(ckd_incidence, 0),
    eskd_defination_1  = replace_na(eskd_defination_1, 0),
    ckd_progression    = replace_na(ckd_progression, 0),
    esrd_kt_after_ici  = replace_na(esrd_kt_after_ici, 0),
    eskd_composite     = ifelse(esrd_kt_after_ici == 1 | eskd_defination_1 == 1, 1, 0),
    eskd_composite_date = pmin(esrd_kt_after_ici_date, eskd_defination_1_date, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Coerce outcome dates
final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(across(
    any_of(c("esrd_kt_after_ici_date", "eskd_defination_1_date",
             "ckd_incidence_date", "ckd_progression_date",
             "eskd_composite_date", "Index_date", "last_cre_date")),
    as.Date
  ))

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
text:
6.4 Time-to-event, composites, survival flags, last_cre_days

final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(
    time_to_eskd_composite  = as.numeric(eskd_composite_date  - Index_date),
    time_to_ckd_incidence   = as.numeric(ckd_incidence_date   - Index_date),
    time_to_ckd_progression = as.numeric(ckd_progression_date - Index_date),
    ckd_composite = ifelse(
      eskd_composite == 1 | ckd_incidence == 1 | ckd_progression == 1, 1, 0
    ),
    time_to_ckd_composite = pmin(
      time_to_eskd_composite, time_to_ckd_incidence,
      time_to_ckd_progression, na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    last_cre_days = as.numeric(last_cre_date - Index_date),
    death_days    = as.numeric(Date_Of_Death - Index_date),
    time_to_death = death_days,
    time_to_death_status = ifelse(!is.na(death_days), 2, 0),
    death         = ifelse(!is.na(Date_Of_Death), 1, 0),
    last_date     = if_else(is.na(Date_Of_Death), last_cre_date, Date_Of_Death),
    last_days     = as.numeric(last_date - Index_date),
    Race = ifelse(Race == "White", "White",
           ifelse(Race == "Black", "Black",
           ifelse(Race == "Asian", "Asian", "Other/Unknown"))),
    Ethnic_Group = case_when(
      Ethnic_Group == "HISPANIC" ~ "Hispanic",
      Ethnic_Group == "Non Hispanic" ~ "Non_hispanic",
      TRUE ~ "Other"
    ),
    # Competing risk: pmin of all event times, then priority-based status
    time_to_ckd_cmp = pmin(time_to_ckd_composite, last_cre_days, death_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    status_cmp = case_when(
      # Priority 1: Death (2)
      !is.na(death_days) & time_to_ckd_cmp == death_days ~ 2,
      # Priority 2: CKD Event (1)
      !is.na(time_to_ckd_composite) & time_to_ckd_cmp == time_to_ckd_composite ~ 1,
      # Priority 3: Censored / Last Creatinine (0)
      !is.na(last_cre_days) & time_to_ckd_cmp == last_cre_days ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(last_cre_days > 0)

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
text:
6.5 Death & survival flags (1–10 years)

for (yr in 1:10) {
  # death_Xyear: strict death only within X years
  final_master[[paste0("death_", yr, "year")]] <-
    ifelse(!is.na(final_master$death_days) & final_master$death_days < 365 * yr, 1, 0)
  # survival_Xyear: last_cre_days >= 365*X (lab follow-up)
  col_name <- paste0("survival_", yr, "year")
  final_master[[col_name]] <- ifelse(final_master$last_cre_days >= 365 * yr, 1, 0)
}

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
text:
6.6 Yearly outcome flags (1–10 years)

for (yr in 1:10) {
  final_master[[paste0("ckd_incidence_", yr, "year")]] <-
    ifelse(final_master$time_to_ckd_incidence < 365 * yr, 1, 0)

  final_master[[paste0("ckd_progression_", yr, "year")]] <-
    ifelse(final_master$time_to_ckd_progression < 365 * yr, 1, 0)

  final_master[[paste0("eskd_composite_", yr, "year")]] <-
    ifelse(final_master$time_to_eskd_composite < 365 * yr, 1, 0)

  final_master[[paste0("ckd_composite_", yr, "year")]] <-
    ifelse(final_master$time_to_ckd_composite < 365 * yr, 1, 0)
}

# Replace NA with 0, then convert to factor
final_master <- final_master %>%
  mutate(across(
    .cols = matches("(ckd_incidence|ckd_progression|eskd_composite|ckd_composite).*year$"),
    .fns  = ~ factor(replace_na(., 0))
  ))

section: 6.7 Yearly CRE medians, eGFR, CKD stage (1–10 years post-index, from RPDR)
text:
6.7 Yearly CRE medians, eGFR, CKD stage (1–10 years post-index, from RPDR)

# Compute yearly median CRE (90-day window around each year mark)
yearly_cre_list <- list()
for (yr in 1:10) {
  yearly_cre_list[[yr]] <- pre_lab_median_year(
    master_lab, year = yr, days = 90,
    index_date = Index_date, Group_Id = "CRE"
  )
}

final_master <- left_join_all(final_master, yearly_cre_list, by = "EMPI")

# Compute eGFR and CKD stage for each year
for (yr in 1:10) {
  cre_col   <- paste0("pre_median_CRE_", yr, "year")
  egfr_col  <- paste0("eGFR_CRE_", yr, "year")
  stage_col <- paste0("ckd_stage_", yr, "year")

  final_master[[egfr_col]]  <- mapply(gfr_calc, final_master[[cre_col]],
                                       final_master$male, final_master$Age)
  final_master[[stage_col]] <- sapply(final_master[[egfr_col]], get_ckd_stage)
}

title: ICI CKD – Long-term Kidney Outcomes Analysis
text:
6.8 AKI (from RPDR Lab)

# AKI: post-baseline CRE > 1.5 × pre-baseline CRE within 90 days (KDIGO grade 2)
aki_data <- master_lab %>%
  merge(pre_lab_baseline, by = "EMPI", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  filter(Group_Id == "CRE", grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Result), !is.na(pre_median_CRE_90days)) %>%
  mutate(Result = as.numeric(Result)) %>%
  filter(Seq_Date_Time > Index_date,
         Seq_Date_Time <= Index_date + 90) %>%
  filter(Result > 1.5 * pre_median_CRE_90days) %>%
  arrange(EMPI, Seq_Date_Time) %>%
  distinct(EMPI, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(EMPI, aki_date = Seq_Date_Time)

final_master <- final_master %>%
  merge(aki_data, by = "EMPI", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    aki = ifelse(!is.na(aki_date), 1, 0),
    aki_days = as.numeric(aki_date - Index_date),
    aki_before_ckd = ifelse(aki_days <= time_to_ckd_composite, 1, 0)
  )

text:
6.9 Cohort exclusion filters

# Exclude: missing baseline CRE, prior ESRD/KT, baseline eGFR < 10
final_master <- final_master %>%
  filter(!is.na(pre_median_CRE_90days), esrd_kt == 0) %>%
  filter(eGFR_CRE_baseline >= 10)

  final_master$male,

title: Propensity-Score Matching – Treated vs Control
text:
Within the 2020–2023 stratum the eligible counts are roughly 1:1.4 (treated 142 vs control 192), so a fixed 1:3 match is structurally infeasible — there simply aren’t 426 controls available. The variable-ratio specification handles this automatically:

2016–2019 era: target up to 1:3 (control supply is plentiful at 777).
2020–2023 era: most treated patients will receive 1:1 matches because min.controls = 1 is the binding constraint once the closest controls are consumed.

This is the right behaviour for this study — it preserves all treated patients, keeps the closest-PS controls in each era, and accepts a smaller k where the data demand it. The downstream Cox / competing-risk model uses subclass-clustered SEs (or MatchIt weights), so unequal cluster sizes are handled correctly.







NotePrerequisite



Before rendering this page, re-render treated_group.qmd and control_group.qmd so the new n_cre_pre_1yr, pre_history_days, has_pre_cre, cre_rate_pre, n_cre_post, cre_rate_post columns are present in the output .xlsx files.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Outcome analyses run on the matched cohort built in Matching (matched_cohort.xlsx). Pipeline mirrors Kavita’s master analysis (Fine-Gray subdistribution + cause-specific Cox + 5-year logistic regression + CIF plots), but uses the propensity-score-matched treated vs control cohort instead of the full ICI-treated cohort.









Outcome
Definition




ckd_composite
Any of CKD incidence, CKD progression, ESKD composite


ckd_incidence
>25% eGFR drop AND eGFR <60, sustained ≥90 days, baseline ≥60


ckd_progression
>30% eGFR drop, sustained ≥90 days, baseline <60


eskd_composite
ESKD by eGFR <10 sustained ≥90 days OR ESRD/KT after index


death
All-cause mortality (time_to_death, death) — no competing risk; KM + standard Cox







Cumulative incidence function (CIF) plot — by treat group, competing risk = death.
Univariate Fine-Gray — treat only.
Multivariate Fine-Gray — treat + Age, sex, white, comorbidities, baseline eGFR, surveillance.
Univariate cause-specific Cox — treat only.
Multivariate cause-specific Cox — same covariates as Fine-Gray multivariate.
5-year logistic regression — same covariates.




treat (1 = ICI-treated, 0 = matched control), Age, male, white, dm, htn, cad, cirrhosis, ppi, steroids, statins, smoking, eGFR_CRE_baseline_decrease_10, n_cre_pre_1yr.
Variables excluded relative to Kavita’s models: ICI_Class, cancer_group, individual chemotherapeutic agents, nephrotoxic_chemo — these are treated-only and cannot be balanced across groups.

5 Cause-specific Cox models
Reports cause-specific HR (95% CI) for the event of interest, treating death as a censoring event.

Code
for (nm in names(outcomes)) {
  o <- outcomes[[nm]]
  d <- build_cmp(m, o$time, o$label) %>%
    mutate(event_only = as.integer(status_cmp == o$label))
  cat("\n\n## ", o$label, "\n\n")

  # Univariate
  uv_form <- as.formula("Surv(time_event, event_only) ~ treat")
  uv_fit  <- coxph(uv_form, data = d)
  cat("**Univariate**\n\n")
  print(uv_fit %>% tbl_regression(exp = TRUE) %>% add_n() %>%
          modify_caption(paste0("Cause-specific Cox — ", o$label, " (univariate)")))

  # Multivariate
  mv_form <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(time_event, event_only) ~ ", mv_rhs))
  mv_fit  <- tryCatch(coxph(mv_form, data = d),
                      error = function(e) { cat("Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })
  if (!is.null(mv_fit)) {
    cat("\n\n**Multivariate**\n\n")
    print(mv_fit %>% tbl_regression(exp = TRUE) %>% add_n() %>%
            modify_caption(paste0("Cause-specific Cox — ", o$label, " (multivariate)")))
  }
}

7 Death (all-cause mortality)
Death is analyzed as its own primary endpoint (no competing risk).

7.1 Kaplan-Meier survival by treat


Code
d_death <- m %>%
  mutate(
    death_event   = as.integer(death == 1),
    time_event    = pmin(time_to_death, last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    time_event_yr = time_event / 365.25,
    death_5year   = as.integer(time_event <= 5 * 365.25 & death_event == 1)
  )

km_fit <- survfit2(Surv(time_event_yr, death_event) ~ treat, data = d_death)

km_fit %>%
  ggsurvfit() +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, limits = c(0, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Kaplan-Meier — All-cause mortality by group",
    x = "Years since Index_date",
    y = "Survival probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

8 Notes

All models adjust for the propensity-score matched cohort on top of the explicit covariates, providing doubly-robust estimates.
Standard errors do not account for matched-pair clustering; for inference critical to publication, refit with cluster(subclass) or use the MatchIt weights with survival::coxph(weights = ...).
Treated-only variables (cancer type/stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapy agents, nephrotoxic_chemo) cannot be included because they have no analogue in the control group; residual confounding by cancer-type is a study limitation.
Death is treated as a competing risk in CIF and Fine-Gray models, and as a censoring event in the cause-specific Cox.
5-year logistic regression complements the time-to-event models with a fixed-horizon interpretation; patients censored before 5y with no event are dropped.

Code
for (nm in names(outcomes)) {
  o <- outcomes[[nm]]
  d <- build_cmp(m, o$time, o$label) %>%
    mutate(event_only = as.integer(status_cmp == o$label))
  cat("\n\n## ", o$label, "\n\n")

  # Univariate
  uv_form <- as.formula("Surv(time_event, event_only) ~ treat")
  uv_fit  <- coxph(uv_form, data = d)
  cat("**Univariate**\n\n")

          modify_caption(paste0("Cause-specific Cox — ", o$label, " (univariate)")))

                      error = function(e) { cat("Failed:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"); NULL })

7 Death (all-cause mortality)
Death is analyzed as its own primary endpoint (no competing risk).

7.1 Kaplan-Meier survival by treat


Code
d_death <- m %>%
  mutate(
    death_event   = as.integer(death == 1),
    time_event    = pmin(time_to_death, last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    time_event_yr = time_event / 365.25,
    death_5year   = as.integer(time_event <= 5 * 365.25 & death_event == 1)
  )

km_fit <- survfit2(Surv(time_event_yr, death_event) ~ treat, data = d_death)

km_fit %>%
  ggsurvfit() +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, limits = c(0, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Kaplan-Meier — All-cause mortality by group",
    x = "Years since Index_date",
    y = "Survival probability"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

8 Notes

All models adjust for the propensity-score matched cohort on top of the explicit covariates, providing doubly-robust estimates.
Standard errors do not account for matched-pair clustering; for inference critical to publication, refit with cluster(subclass) or use the MatchIt weights with survival::coxph(weights = ...).
Treated-only variables (cancer type/stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapy agents, nephrotoxic_chemo) cannot be included because they have no analogue in the control group; residual confounding by cancer-type is a study limitation.
Death is treated as a competing risk in CIF and Fine-Gray models, and as a censoring event in the cause-specific Cox.
5-year logistic regression complements the time-to-event models with a fixed-horizon interpretation; patients censored before 5y with no event are dropped.

8 Notes

All models adjust for the propensity-score matched cohort on top of the explicit covariates, providing doubly-robust estimates.
Standard errors do not account for matched-pair clustering; for inference critical to publication, refit with cluster(subclass) or use the MatchIt weights with survival::coxph(weights = ...).
Treated-only variables (cancer type/stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapy agents, nephrotoxic_chemo) cannot be included because they have no analogue in the control group; residual confounding by cancer-type is a study limitation.
Death is treated as a competing risk in CIF and Fine-Gray models, and as a censoring event in the cause-specific Cox.
5-year logistic regression complements the time-to-event models with a fixed-horizon interpretation; patients censored before 5y with no event are dropped.

7 Death (all-cause mortality)
Death is analyzed as its own primary endpoint (no competing risk).

7.1 Kaplan-Meier survival by treat


Code
d_death <- m %>%
  mutate(
    death_event   = as.integer(death == 1),
    time_event    = pmin(time_to_death, last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    time_event_yr = time_event / 365.25,
    death_5year   = as.integer(time_event <= 5 * 365.25 & death_event == 1)

km_fit %>%

  add_confidence_interval() +

8 Notes

All models adjust for the propensity-score matched cohort on top of the explicit covariates, providing doubly-robust estimates.
Standard errors do not account for matched-pair clustering; for inference critical to publication, refit with cluster(subclass) or use the MatchIt weights with survival::coxph(weights = ...).
Treated-only variables (cancer type/stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapy agents, nephrotoxic_chemo) cannot be included because they have no analogue in the control group; residual confounding by cancer-type is a study limitation.
Death is treated as a competing risk in CIF and Fine-Gray models, and as a censoring event in the cause-specific Cox.
5-year logistic regression complements the time-to-event models with a fixed-horizon interpretation; patients censored before 5y with no event are dropped.

7 Death (all-cause mortality)
Death is analyzed as its own primary endpoint (no competing risk).

7.1 Kaplan-Meier survival by treat


Code
d_death <- m %>%
  mutate(
    death_event   = as.integer(death == 1),
    time_event    = pmin(time_to_death, last_cre_days, na.rm = TRUE),
    time_event_yr = time_event / 365.25,
    death_5year   = as.integer(time_event <= 5 * 365.25 & death_event == 1)
  )

km_fit <- survfit2(Surv(time_event_yr, death_event) ~ treat, data = d_death)

km_fit %>%
  ggsurvfit() +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:10, limits = c(0, 10)) +
  labs(
    title = "Kaplan-Meier — All-cause mortality by group",
    x = "Years since Index_date",

  theme_minimal()

8 Notes

All models adjust for the propensity-score matched cohort on top of the explicit covariates, providing doubly-robust estimates.
Standard errors do not account for matched-pair clustering; for inference critical to publication, refit with cluster(subclass) or use the MatchIt weights with survival::coxph(weights = ...).
Treated-only variables (cancer type/stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapy agents, nephrotoxic_chemo) cannot be included because they have no analogue in the control group; residual confounding by cancer-type is a study limitation.
Death is treated as a competing risk in CIF and Fine-Gray models, and as a censoring event in the cause-specific Cox.
5-year logistic regression complements the time-to-event models with a fixed-horizon interpretation; patients censored before 5y with no event are dropped.

8 Notes

All models adjust for the propensity-score matched cohort on top of the explicit covariates, providing doubly-robust estimates.
Standard errors do not account for matched-pair clustering; for inference critical to publication, refit with cluster(subclass) or use the MatchIt weights with survival::coxph(weights = ...).
Treated-only variables (cancer type/stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapy agents, nephrotoxic_chemo) cannot be included because they have no analogue in the control group; residual confounding by cancer-type is a study limitation.
Death is treated as a competing risk in CIF and Fine-Gray models, and as a censoring event in the cause-specific Cox.
5-year logistic regression complements the time-to-event models with a fixed-horizon interpretation; patients censored before 5y with no event are dropped.

8.1 Build per-lab eGFR dataframe

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(lme4)
  library(lmerTest)
})

# CKD-EPI 2021 creatinine-only (race-free)
ckd_epi_gfr <- function(creat, male, age) {
  k <- ifelse(male == 1, 0.9, 0.7)
  a <- ifelse(male == 1, -0.302, -0.241)
  m <- ifelse(male == 1, 1, 1.012)
  142 * pmin(creat / k, 1)^a * pmax(creat / k, 1)^-1.2 * 0.9938^age * m
}

# Treated RPDR Lab
t_lab <- read.table(
  "/Users/to909/Partners HealthCare Dropbox/Tianqi Ouyang/CKD after ICI/RPDR/mes98_093025104659807332_Lab.txt",
  sep = "|", fill = TRUE, quote = "", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  select(EMPI, Seq_Date_Time, Result, Group_Id) %>%
  filter(Group_Id == "CRE", grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
  mutate(
    Seq_Date_Time = as.Date(Seq_Date_Time, "%m/%d/%Y"),
    Result        = as.numeric(Result)
  )

# Control RPDR Lab (04092026 pull)
c_lab <- read.table(
  "/Users/to909/Partners HealthCare Dropbox/Tianqi Ouyang/CKD after ICI/RPDR/RPDR Joyita/04092026/mes98_040726114217167239_Lab.txt",
  sep = "|", fill = TRUE, quote = "", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  select(EMPI, Seq_Date_Time, Result, Group_Id) %>%
  filter(Group_Id == "CRE", grepl("^\\d+\\.\\d+$", Result)) %>%
  mutate(
    Seq_Date_Time = as.Date(Seq_Date_Time, "%m/%d/%Y"),
    Result        = as.numeric(Result)
  )

# Per-patient anchor (Age, male, Index_date, treat) — one row per EMPI
anchor <- m %>%
  distinct(EMPI, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(Index_date = as.Date(Index_date)) %>%
  select(EMPI, treat, male, Age, Index_date, last_cre_days)

# Join labs to anchor based on treat
labs <- bind_rows(
  t_lab %>% inner_join(anchor %>% filter(treat == "ICI Treated"), by = "EMPI"),
  c_lab %>% inner_join(anchor %>% filter(treat == "Control"),     by = "EMPI")
) %>%
  filter(Seq_Date_Time > Index_date) %>%
  mutate(
    days_since_index = as.numeric(Seq_Date_Time - Index_date),
    year_since_index = days_since_index / 365.25,
    eGFR_CRE         = ckd_epi_gfr(Result, male, Age + year_since_index)

# Marginal (fixed-effects-only) prediction with 95% CI from an lmer fit.
# Returns a data.frame: year_since_index, treat, fit, lo, hi.
lmer_marginal_pred <- function(fit, year_grid) {
  grid <- expand.grid(
    year_since_index = year_grid,
    treat            = c("Control", "ICI Treated"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  grid$treat <- factor(grid$treat, levels = c("Control", "ICI Treated"))

  mm <- model.matrix(~ year_since_index * treat, data = grid)
  fe <- lme4::fixef(fit)
  grid$fit <- as.numeric(mm %*% fe)
  v  <- mm %*% as.matrix(vcov(fit)) %*% t(mm)
  grid$se <- sqrt(diag(v))
  grid$lo <- grid$fit - 1.96 * grid$se
  grid$hi <- grid$fit + 1.96 * grid$se
  grid
}

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Study population
Adult patients who received immune-checkpoint-inhibitor (ICI) therapy at Mass General Brigham between 2016 and 2023 (n = 379) were compared with a contemporaneous non-ICI control cohort of patients with a primary neoplasm diagnosis (ICD-10 C00–D49) identified from the Research Patient Data Registry (RPDR). The index date was defined as the first ICI dose for the treated group and the first qualifying neoplasm-diagnosis date for the control group. Cohort inclusion criteria for both groups required (i) a baseline serum creatinine within 12 months prior to the index date, (ii) at least two post-index creatinine measurements, (iii) ≥ 18 months of follow-up, and (iv) a baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ≥ 10 mL/min/1.73 m². Controls with an index date before 2016 (n = 338) were excluded a priori because they had no temporal counterpart in the treated cohort. After all inclusion and exclusion criteria, 379 treated and 969 control patients were eligible for matching.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Propensity-score matching
Treatment-effect estimation used a propensity-score (PS) matched cohort to mitigate baseline imbalance. The PS for receiving ICI therapy was estimated using multivariable logistic regression with the following pre-index covariates: age, male sex, white race (binary), diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, cirrhosis, baseline use of proton-pump inhibitors, systemic corticosteroids, statins, and active smoking; the baseline CKD-EPI 2021 eGFR (creatinine-only, race-free); and the number of pre-index creatinine measurements within 365 days (n_cre_pre_1yr) as an explicit adjustment for differential ascertainment intensity. Variable-ratio 1:k nearest-neighbor matching was performed with MatchIt (R) using the logit of the propensity score, no replacement, a caliper of 0.2 × SD(logit PS) (Austin 2011), exact matching on calendar era (2016–2019 vs 2020–2023), and ratio = 2, min.controls = 1, max.controls = 3 to maintain feasibility in the 2020–2023 stratum where the control pool was structurally limited. Balance was assessed by standardized mean differences (SMDs), with a target of |SMD| < 0.1 for all matching variables.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Outcomes
Five outcomes were analyzed: (1) CKD composite (CKD incidence, CKD progression, or ESKD composite); (2) CKD incidence (>25% relative eGFR drop and eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m² sustained ≥ 90 days, in patients with baseline eGFR ≥ 60); (3) CKD progression (>30% relative eGFR drop sustained ≥ 90 days in patients with baseline eGFR < 60); (4) ESKD composite (eGFR < 10 sustained ≥ 90 days or documented end-stage renal disease / kidney transplant after the index date); and (5) all-cause mortality. Time-to-event was measured in days from the index date, with administrative censoring at the last available creatinine date (last_cre_days). All eGFR values were computed with the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine-only equation (Inker et al. 2021), which is race-free.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Time-to-event modelling of CKD/ESKD outcomes
For each CKD/ESKD endpoint, death was treated as a competing risk. Cumulative incidence functions (CIFs) were estimated non-parametrically using the Aalen–Johansen estimator (tidycmprsk::cuminc) and plotted with 95% point-wise confidence intervals. Subdistribution hazard ratios were estimated with Fine–Gray models (tidycmprsk::crr) in unadjusted and adjusted forms. The adjusted model included treatment group plus age, male sex, white race, diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, cirrhosis, baseline PPI / steroid / statin use, smoking, baseline eGFR (expressed per 10-mL decrement: eGFR_CRE_baseline_decrease_10), and n_cre_pre_1yr. Cause-specific hazard ratios were estimated with Cox proportional-hazards models (survival::coxph), censoring death; the same covariate set was used. The proportional-hazards assumption was inspected by Schoenfeld residuals.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
All-cause mortality
Survival was summarised by Kaplan–Meier estimation (survfit2). Hazard ratios for mortality were estimated with Cox proportional-hazards models, treating death as the primary event without competing risk.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Fixed-horizon (5-year) analyses
In parallel with the time-to-event models, 5-year event probabilities were modelled by logistic regression for each outcome (univariate and multivariate using the same covariate set). Patients censored before 5 years without the event were excluded from the 5-year denominator.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Longitudinal eGFR slope
To quantify annual eGFR decline between groups, every post-index serum-creatinine measurement was extracted from the RPDR Lab files and converted to an eGFR with CKD-EPI 2021, advancing chronologic age to the lab date (treated: 9,455 observations; control: 11,148 observations). Three linear mixed-effects models (lme4::lmer, REML, bobyqa optimizer; Satterthwaite degrees of freedom via lmerTest) were fit:

Long-term: all post-index observations, eGFR ~ time × treat + (time | EMPI) — random intercept and slope per patient.
First-year: observations within 365 days of index, eGFR ~ time × treat + (1 | EMPI) — random intercept only (slope not identifiable because 55 % of controls had only one first-year measurement).
Three-year: observations within 1095 days, eGFR ~ time × treat + (time | EMPI) — random intercept and slope.

In each model the time × treat interaction term is the between-group difference in annual eGFR decline (mL/min/1.73 m² per year). Each model’s group-mean trajectory is visualised with the fixed-effects marginal prediction (and 95% CI ribbon) from the fitted lmer — no LOESS smoother, no per-patient slope plot.

title: Results — Outcome Analyses on Matched Cohort
text:
Software and inference
All analyses were performed in R using MatchIt, survival, tidycmprsk, lme4, lmerTest, ggsurvfit, gtsummary, cobalt, and tidyverse. Two-sided p-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant. Standard errors in the matched-cohort outcome models do not explicitly account for the matched-pair clustering induced by 1:k matching; sensitivity analyses with subclass-clustered robust standard errors (coxph(... , cluster = subclass)) or MatchIt matching weights are planned for the final manuscript. Treated-only covariates (cancer type and stage, ICI class, individual chemotherapeutic agents, nephrotoxic chemotherapy flag) have no analogue in the control group and were therefore excluded from the PS model and outcome adjustment; this is acknowledged as a source of residual confounding by indication.
